title: CPP v0.1 Claim-Preservation Result
description: Machine-readable result of evaluating one claim transformation against the Claim Preservation Profile v0.1. The result is a statement about claim-preservation behaviour only. It is not a statement that the underlying system is safe, correct, aligned, or compliant, and it is not a statement that the recorded facts are true.

relation.description: Claim-relation vocabulary of CPP v0.1 section 4. NOT_MEASURED, INCONCLUSIVE and ERROR are non-success states and MUST NOT be read as passing, equivalent, or narrower.

passing_relation.description: The subset of relations that may be treated as claim-preserving. Provided so implementations do not each invent their own passing set.

measurement_state.description: Whether a dimension was actually measured. Absence of measurement is never a positive result.

ref.description: Stable identifier of the evidence artifact.

digest.description: Content digest of the artifact as retrieved, or null if not retrieved.

resolved.description: Whether the reference was actually dereferenced. null means unknown.

verified.description: Whether the artifact was verified. Per CPP-7 an unfetched, unfetchable, redacted, or unverified artifact MUST NOT be reported as verified. null means unknown, not verified.

assurance.description: How the artifact is attested. Per CPP-8, integrity attributes do not establish the truth of the recorded fact.

dimension_result.description: Result for one independent strength dimension. Dimensions are evaluated separately and are NOT combined into a single scalar claim-strength score; the model is a partial order (CPP v0.1 section 2 and 5).

status.description: Direction of change on this dimension, using the same vocabulary as the overall relation.

input_value.description: Dimension value of the input claim, if represented.

output_value.description: Dimension value of the output claim, if represented.

supporting_evidence.description: Evidence relied on for this dimension. MUST be non-empty when status is SUPPORTED_STRENGTHENING.

qualification.description: What limits this dimension result. Free text intended to be shown wherever the result is shown (CPP-20).

basis.description: The exact rule or heuristic that produced this dimension result, so the result is auditable.

allOf.description: The converse: a dimension that was not measured, was inconclusive, or errored must not carry a claim-preserving status. Without this, a result could report EQUIVALENT on every dimension while having measured none of them.

cpp_version.description: Version of the Claim Preservation Profile this result was produced against.

case_id.description: Identifier of the evaluated transformation case or fixture.

relation.description: Overall claim relation between input and output. This is a summary of the dimension results and MUST NOT be more favourable than the dimensions support. If any evaluated dimension is AMPLIFIED_UNSUPPORTED, the overall relation MUST be AMPLIFIED_UNSUPPORTED or INCOMPARABLE, never a passing relation.

input_claim_ref.description: Reference to the input claim C_in. Required for provenance continuity (CPP-6).

output_claim_ref.description: Reference to the output claim C_out.

dimensions.description: Per-dimension results. Keys are dimension names; CPP v0.1 section 5 lists the dimensions an implementation SHOULD evaluate. Dimensions are kept separate on purpose: no scalar collapse.

added_evidence.description: Evidence introduced by this transformation, as distinct from evidence inherited from the input claim. Strengthening is only supportable by evidence listed here (CPP-1).

violations.description: CPP requirements violated by this transformation. Empty array means no violation was detected by the evaluated checks; it does not mean every requirement was checked. See dimensions[].measurement_state and coverage.

observer_effect.description: Observer/probe-effect assessment (CPP-15, CPP-16, CPP-17). Required even when nothing was measured; in that case the states say so explicitly.

subject_awareness.description: Whether the observed system can detect that it is under evaluation or observation.

observer_is_intervention.description: True when the observing component also changes policy, control state, permissions, or model context (CPP-16).

perturbation_nonclaims.description: What the observation cannot establish because of the way it was observed.

generalizes_to_uninstrumented.description: Whether the result may be generalized to the uninstrumented condition. MUST NOT be YES when execution_interference is NOT_MEASURED or INCONCLUSIVE (CPP-15).

qualifications.description: Material qualifications that constrain the output claim. Per CPP-20 these MUST travel with the result wherever it is displayed or exported.

non_claims.description: What this result explicitly does not establish. Per CPP-4 an empty array is not a discharge of the input claim's non-claims; discharge must be recorded in violations or in added_evidence.

evidence_refs.description: All evidence referenced by the output claim, inherited and added.

basis.description: The exact, pinned basis of this evaluation (CPP-13). A moving reference such as 'latest' does not support a reproducibility claim.

pinned.description: False when any input of the evaluation was a moving reference. A frozen reproducibility claim MUST NOT be made when this is false.

coverage.description: Which CPP requirements this evaluation actually examined. Requirements absent from 'evaluated' were not checked and MUST NOT be reported as satisfied.

allOf.description: A non-empty violation list can never accompany a passing relation.
Strengthening must be attributable to identifiable added evidence (CPP-1).
An unsupported amplification on any single dimension sinks the overall relation. This enforces the rule stated on the 'relation' property rather than leaving it to prose.
A dimension that was not measured, was inconclusive, or errored blocks a claim-preserving overall relation. The overall relation may never be more favourable than the dimensions support.
